clue.text: Writer of translation seen in home counties

indicators.note: the translation is seen sitting inside the home counties, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, where the home counties around London lie
a crib is a literal translation used by students, often illicitly

explanation.surface: A translator is spotted living in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties surrounding London, in south-east England; a crib is schoolboy slang for a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist or professional penman, someone whose job is writing.

clue.text: Quiet walks may be such a muddle

parts.note: sh is the sound used to call for quiet
ambles means strolls or walks at leisure

explanation.surface: Strolling about quietly may leave things in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles is a scene of total disorder, a mess or confusion.

clue.text: It may be dearer if refined

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow may be turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something might cost more once it has been purified.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied means lofty and exclusive, elevated above the common, a near synonym of polished or cultivated.

parts.note: reads as a child being told to go out and play, but means performing music in public for coins

explanation.definitionFit: Busking is performing music outdoors for donations from passers-by.

parts.note: slips are small errors

indicators.note: the note is sent back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Sloppy errors in a written memo come back to the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' sends the note backwards; doh is the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod describes work done hastily without care, sloppy.

clue.text: Honestly, real problems for these loveless people

indicators.note: the words are given problems, so they are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An agony aunt frankly admits that lonely singles have real troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are single people seeking love, as in newspaper personal ads.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a loop is a ring or circle

explanation.surface: Telephone the local swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like a phone call; instead LOOP, a ring, is read upwards to give POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a tank of water for swimming in, a swimming bath.

explanation.surface: A rural community stages a dramatic production.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village; Hamlet is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince.

clue.text: Brave US prosecutor overcomes criminal gang

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming over means sitting on top of, so the prosecutor goes above the gang

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor
a ring is an organised group of criminals

explanation.surface: A courageous American attorney defeats a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring means bold and fearless, willing to take risks.

clue.text: A vote going from one side to the other

definitions.text: going from one side to the other

parts.note: a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: A ballot that sees a politician change parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Across means from one side over to the opposite side.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
former means previous or of old

explanation.surface: A storyteller who was once well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer tells tales on others to the authorities, a sneak or grass.

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so we take its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: an Indian is an Asian

explanation.surface: A professional cricketer in a Test match hears an Indian player declare the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' makes ASIAN sound like the ending spelt ATION. A Test is a full international cricket match, and 'declaration' is also cricket's word for closing an innings, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a solemn affirmation or statement, a formal avowal.

explanation.surface: An enthusiast is a pale golden colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast, as in film buff; buff is also a pale yellowish-brown colour.

explanation.surface: Question the chef.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill is to question intensely, and also to cook under direct heat.

clue.text: Like Scrooge, getting a bad name

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt or corrupted, so the word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dickens's miser earns himself a poor reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge is the miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean means stingy or miserly, unwilling to spend money.

clue.text: Taking up drink befitting a king

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking the word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Starting to drink in a style suitable for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, fit for a monarch.

explanation.surface: Is the baby's stroller full of insects?
explanation.definitionFit: A buggy is a lightweight pushchair; buggy also means crawling with bugs.

explanation.surface: Something left to the last moment, well after ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hour is the last possible moment; literally it is the hour after the tenth.

explanation.surface: Laying in a stock of socks and tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking means filling with goods; a stocking is a close-fitting leg garment, an item of hosiery.

clue.text: Sign of Muslims in suburban street

explanation.surface: A symbol of Islam appears on a residential road.
explanation.definitionFit: The crescent moon is an emblem of Islam; a crescent is also a curved row of houses.

parts.note: a chap is a man, here possessive
chortling is gleeful laughing, laughter

explanation.surface: A grave offence, yet the fellow keeps chuckling.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is unlawful killing without intent, a grave felony.

clue.text: Malayan clothing seen to hang loosely round Ron

indicators.note: the drooping word goes round the name, enclosing it

parts.note: to sag is to droop or hang down loosely
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrap from Malaya appears to droop around a man called Ron.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a wrapped skirt-like garment worn in Malaysia and Indonesia.

clue.text: Piece of equipment likely to snap

definitions.text: Piece of equipment likely to snap

parts.words: Piece of equipment likely to snap
parts.note: suggests a fragile tool that breaks easily, but snap means take a photograph

explanation.definitionFit: A device for taking photographs takes snaps, quick pictures.

indicators.note: backed means the words are run backwards, both pieces together

parts.note: to bar is to block or obstruct

explanation.surface: Get in the way of someone's betting choice at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses BAR plus A, BARA, to give the result; the surface pretends a punter has backed a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of fine, spirited horse.

explanation.surface: Dirt on our world.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is soil or ground; Earth is also our planet.

clue.text: On stage, performs a bit of Scripture

explanation.surface: An actor in the theatre presents part of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor acts on stage; Acts is a book of the New Testament.

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
an ass is a silly person

explanation.surface: Hand authority over to an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to hand on or transfer something to another.

indicators.note: the word for always follows on after the abbreviation for page

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A young servant is forever trailing after a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, such as a duke or earl.

clue.text: Get some no-hoper a ticket for noted performance

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: Buy a pessimist a theatre pass for a celebrated show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' is musical: a performance in notes, as in opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic means relating to opera, where the performance is sung to music.

explanation.surface: Contaminate the ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make dirty or corrupt; a defile is a narrow mountain pass.

clue.text: Granny is moving to lawyers' place

indicators.note: the letters are on the move, shifting into a new order

explanation.surface: Grandmother is relocating to a legal district.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London, where barristers train and work.
explanation.definitionFit: This London Inn of Court houses barristers' chambers.

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the battle, inside it

parts.note: a fight is a battle
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Charging into combat full of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Fright is sudden terror or alarm.
